verdict.rationale: Community users say Name.com supports two-factor/multi-factor authentication. The docs show API tokens issued from a Security settings page, with separate development and production tokens and reseller sub-accounts that have their own credentials and permissions. However, the API uses HTTP Basic Auth, and nothing shows per-token permission scoping or IP allowlisting. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of 2FA, per-token scoped API permissions, IP allowlisting on API access, and independent hands-on corroboration of these controls.
